To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flexible GnRH antagonist regimen, when used in a group of women undergoing their first IVF/ICSI cycle, was not associated with an increased risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, nor with a reduced oocyte retrieval rate, when compared with a GnRH agonist long protocol.
the use of the GnRH antagonist protocol in patients undergoing ovarian stimulation for IVF results in higher pregnancy and live birth rates compared to the long protocol with a GnRH agonist.
the flexible GnRH antagonist IVF cycle protocol is associated with higher oocyte yield and higher pregnancy rate than the conventional GnRH agonist protocol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a GnRH antagonist in a flexible long protocol for ovarian stimulation in IVF.
the effects of GnRH antagonists in a flexible GnRH antagonist regimen on the oocyte quality in IVF/ICSI cycles.
the effects of GnRHa and GnRH antagonist on ovarian function in the female rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flexible protocol of GnRH antagonist is a safe, effective and feasible protocol for IVF/ICSI.
in patients undergoing IVF/ICSI with a flexible GnRH antagonist regimen, a higher serum LH concentration on the day of triggering oocyte matuation with hCG is associated with a lower oocyte yield.
the use of GnRH antagonists in ART is safe and effective and should be considered as a first-line approach for ovarian stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the circulating LH level after triggering oocytes to mature with GnRH agonists (GnRHa) may predict the oocyte yield in the flexible GnRH antagonist (GnRHA) protocol.
the flexible antagonist protocol is a safe and effective protocol for IVF, with a high rate of pregnancy, a low rate of OHSS and a low incidence of cycle cancellation.
the circulating LH levels after triggering oocyte maturity may predict oocyte production and fertilization rate in the flexible GnRH agonist protocol.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a flexible GnRH antagonist regimen with a fixed 0.25 mg dose of triptorelin may be associated with a higher number of oocytes and better embryo quality compared with a fixed 3 mg dose of tripterelin.
